context: Force-directed network graph showing skill co-occurrence across 105 D3.js blocks, with nodes sized by frequency and colored by skill category
first_impression: The dark constellation aesthetic is thematically coherent with glowing nodes and a deliberate multi-color palette, but the force layout leaves the main cluster off-center with isolated nodes adrift in empty space
what_works: The hover interaction — fading unconnected nodes and highlighting edges in the hovered node's color — is well-executed and satisfying; the 7-color categorical palette against the dark background is intentional and harmonious, reinforcing the constellation theme without resorting to schemeCategory10 defaults
what_doesnt: The force simulation produces poor space utilization: isolated low-degree nodes (data-gathering, webgl) float far from the main cluster leaving large empty quadrants, and the cluster itself sits right-of-center rather than filling the viewport; the label threshold (count >= 9) leaves several visible medium-sized nodes unlabeled, making the graph unreadable without hovering
